make_project_flow <- function(language = "en") {
  if (language == "en") {
    labels <- list(
      params = "Explicit parameters\\nScripts + notebook",
      raw = "data/raw/twitter/\\nOpinion + president corpora",
      scripts = "scripts/data/ingest_market.R\\nManual market refresh",
      processed = "data/processed/\\nTwo stable master datasets",
      notebook = "notebooks + paper\\nMethodological interpretation",
      outputs = "output/figures/español/\\noutput/tables/español/",
      docs = "README + docs/paper/\\nReproducible documentation",
      run = "BanRep + XM online sources\\nTRM, COLCAP, TES, energy"
    )
    file_stub <- "readme_project_flow_en"
  } else {
    labels <- list(
      params = "Parametros explicitos\\nScripts + cuaderno",
      raw = "data/raw/\\nSnapshots de tweets + mercado",
      scripts = "scripts/data/ingest_market.R\\nActualizacion manual mercado",
      processed = "data/processed/\\nDos contratos master",
      notebook = "notebooks/español/\\nCuaderno metodológico del paper",
      outputs = "output/figures/español/\\noutput/tables/español/",
      docs = "README + docs/paper/\\nDocumentación reproducible",
      run = "Notebook self-contained\\nNo external source()"
    )
    file_stub <- "readme_project_flow_es"
  }

  dot <- sprintf(
    'digraph project_flow {
      graph [rankdir = LR, bgcolor = "transparent", pad = "0.35", nodesep = "0.55", ranksep = "0.75", charset = "UTF-8"]
      node [shape = rectangle, style = "rounded,filled", fontname = "Helvetica", fontsize = 18, penwidth = 1.4, margin = "0.12,0.08"]
      edge [color = "#52616b", penwidth = 2.2, arrowsize = 0.75]

      params    [label = "%s", fillcolor = "#eaf2f8", color = "#2c6f9e"]
      raw       [label = "%s", fillcolor = "#f6eddc", color = "#b87918"]
      scripts   [label = "%s", fillcolor = "#e8f3ea", color = "#2f7d50"]
      processed [label = "%s", fillcolor = "#f3eef8", color = "#7656a3"]
      notebook  [label = "%s", fillcolor = "#fff5f2", color = "#bd5d38"]
      outputs   [label = "%s", fillcolor = "#edf7f7", color = "#2a7a80"]
      docs      [label = "%s", fillcolor = "#f4f4f4", color = "#555555"]
      run       [label = "%s", shape = note, fillcolor = "#ffffff", color = "#2f2f2f"]

      params -> scripts
      params -> notebook
      raw -> scripts
      run -> scripts
      scripts -> processed
      processed -> notebook
      notebook -> outputs
      processed -> outputs
      notebook -> docs
      outputs -> docs
    }',
    labels$params, labels$raw, labels$scripts, labels$processed,
    labels$notebook, labels$outputs, labels$docs, labels$run
  )

  graph <- DiagrammeR::grViz(dot)
  svg <- DiagrammeRsvg::export_svg(graph)
  svg_path <- file.path(asset_dir, paste0(file_stub, ".svg"))
  png_path <- file.path(asset_dir, paste0(file_stub, ".png"))
  writeLines(svg, svg_path, useBytes = TRUE)
  rsvg::rsvg_png(charToRaw(svg), png_path, width = 1800, height = 1000)
  png_path
}

project_flow_path <- make_project_flow("en")

  ),
  max_depth = 2,
  show_hidden = FALSE,
  project = "none",
  format = "ascii",
  return_lines = TRUE
)

# Economic Impact of President Petro's Tweets

```{=html}
<p>
  <img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/R-4.x-276DC3?logo=r&logoColor=white" alt="R">
  <img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/R%20Markdown-reproducible-75AADB?logo=r&logoColor=white" alt="R Markdown">
  <img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/notebook-autocontained%20analysis-2f7d50" alt="Autocontained notebook">
  <img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/market%20data-manual%20update-bd5d38" alt="Manual market update">
  <img src="https://img.shields.io/badge/outputs-figures%20%2B%20gt%20tables-2a7a80" alt="Outputs">
</p>
```

This repository updates the paper **`Impacto_discurso_petro__ENG_`** by
studying whether Twitter/X discussion around Colombian President Gustavo
Petro is associated with short-run movements in Colombian financial
indicators.

The project is now organized as a reproducible R workflow for the
**August 2022-May 2026** monthly tweet snapshots. The current design
separates two corpora: `opinion`, with public discussion about Petro in
`data/raw/twitter/Opinión sobre Petro/`, and `presidente`, with tweets
written by `@petrogustavo` in
`data/raw/twitter/Tweets de Gustavo Petro/`. The financial block uses
`TRM` as the exchange-rate series, `COLCAP` as the main stock-market
proxy, peso-denominated zero-coupon `TES` rates as the sovereign
fixed-income block, and XM's daily weighted national energy spot price
as the electricity-market series. Those market series are downloaded as
raw official CSVs into `data/raw/market/`. The processing script then
consolidates all inputs into two stable contracts in `data/processed/`;
download and provenance audits are written under `output/tables/español/`.
The original 2023 paper remains available as
conceptual and historical context in
[`docs/paper/Impacto_discurso_petro__ENG_.pdf`](docs/paper/Impacto_discurso_petro__ENG_.pdf).
The active paper is a Quarto manuscript that updates the narrative with
`quanteda`-style networks, EDA of presidential tweet frequency,
sentiment, topics, and exploratory financial diagnostics.

## Project Overview {#project-overview}

**Research question.** Do presidential tweets and related public
discussion produce measurable short-run movements in Colombian financial
markets?

The updated analysis focuses on:

- daily tweet frequency and metadata quality;
- daily, weekly, and monthly frequency of tweets issued by
  `@petrogustavo`;
- hashtags, mentions, co-mentions, and lexical co-occurrence networks;
- hashtag and mention networks using the visual style of the official
  `quanteda` Twitter example;
- word clouds by corpus, time, themes, sentiment, topics, and network
  communities;
- temporal TF-IDF evolution as supporting evidence for the word-stream
  view;
- weakly supervised thematic classification with holdout evaluation;
- Spanish NRC sentiment, polarity, and daily weighted sentiment;
- text mining with `quanteda`, `quanteda.textstats`, and
  `quanteda.textplots`;
- Wordfish scaling with `quanteda.textmodels`;
- topic modeling with `stm`;
- stationarity diagnostics, Granger tests, and VAR diagnostics for
  `TRM`, `COLCAP`, `TES 10Y`, the `TES 10Y - TES 1Y` slope, and XM
  energy price.

The current workflow uses BanRep official series for `TRM`, `COLCAP`,
and `TES`, and XM official energy spot price data; the active analysis
no longer depends on the older equity proxy used in the original case
study.

## Methodological Traceability {#methodological-traceability}

### Where are parameters and sources defined?

The project no longer uses a separate YAML configuration file. The data
scripts define their dates, paths, source IDs, endpoints, and reference
URLs explicitly at the top of each script, while the notebook places
each analytical constant next to its first consumer. Market refresh
provenance is persisted under `output/tables/español/`.

### What is the role of `scripts/`?

The main analysis is intentionally self-contained in
`notebooks/español/Cuaderno_Paper_Español.Rmd`. Functions for cleaning,
classification, visualization, NLP, networks, series, econometrics, and
model validation live in the notebook.

Two scripts are expected before rendering when inputs need refreshing:
`scripts/data/ingest_market.R` downloads official raw market series, and
`scripts/data/twitter_process_raw_data.R` validates and writes
`tweets_master.csv` and `market_master.csv`. The notebook reads only
those two contracts; it does not execute external scripts.

Recommended execution order:

1.  Update market data manually only when needed.
2.  Run `Rscript scripts/data/twitter_process_raw_data.R` to prepare raw
    Twitter and market data.
3.  Confirm the required CSVs exist in `data/processed/`.
4.  Render `notebooks/español/Cuaderno_Paper_Español.Rmd`.
5.  Review generated figures and tables under `output/`.

### Does the notebook depend on `source()`?

No. The notebook defines the helpers it needs in its setup chunk and
consumes the prepared CSVs under `data/processed/`. It may recompute
text analysis, tables, figures, network summaries, and econometric
diagnostics for traceability, but it does not call external scripts.

### How are market data extracted, and how do raw and processed files differ?

The main market series are extracted with the manual updater
`scripts/data/ingest_market.R`, which can be run as
`Rscript scripts/data/ingest_market.R`. It calls Banco de la República
services: SDMX/graficador for TRM, COLCAP, and zero-coupon TES rates,
and the XM SINERGOX daily API for `PPPrecBolsNaci`. Endpoints, series
IDs, and reference URLs are defined in the script constants and recorded
in `output/tables/español/ingesta_mercado_fuentes.csv`. Therefore
`data/raw/market/` stores the raw official series (`*_raw.csv`), while
`data/processed/market_master.csv` stores the validated daily panel.

Market traceability lives in:

- `data/processed/market_master.csv`: daily series used in models.
- `output/tables/español/ingesta_mercado_fuentes.csv`: `retrieved_at`, `source_url`,
  `source_series_id`, `source_series_name`, `status`, and extraction
  messages.
- `output/tables/español/ingesta_mercado_cobertura.csv`: expected days, observed days,
  `coverage_ratio`, and coverage status.

For a closed replication snapshot, freeze both master CSVs together
with the raw market inputs and refresh audits.

## Installation {#installation}

Install R and the R packages used by the manual market updater,
notebook, and README rendering. From the repository root:

``` r
install.packages(c(
  "readr", "readxl", "dplyr", "tidyr", "stringr", "lubridate",
  "purrr", "ggplot2", "ggwordcloud", "httr2", "xml2", "jsonlite", "syuzhet", "lmtest", "zoo", "scales",
  "janitor", "tibble", "quanteda", "quanteda.textstats",
  "quanteda.textplots", "quanteda.textmodels", "sentometrics", "stm",
  "igraph", "ggraph", "tidygraph", "vars", "tseries", "urca", "sandwich",
  "forcats", "rmarkdown", "knitr", "here", "DiagrammeR", "DiagrammeRsvg", "rsvg",
  "ragg", "spacyr", "reticulate", "fs", "glue"
))

install.packages(
  "printtree",
  repos = c("https://cran.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org")
)
```

The user-facing README request referred to `printree`. The currently
available R package is `printtree`; the Rmd checks for `printree` first
and then uses `printtree` as the compatible implementation.

## Reproduce the Analysis {#reproduce-the-analysis}

The notebook is the primary analysis surface. Before rendering, confirm
the two data contracts exist under `data/processed/`; refresh market
data manually only when the official series need updating:

- `data/processed/tweets_master.csv`
- `data/processed/market_master.csv`
- figures under `output/figures/español/`
- static HTML and CSV tables under `output/tables/español/`

`data/processed/` intentionally excludes analytical products such as
daily sentiment, corpus comparison tables, model datasets, and Granger
diagnostics. Those are built inside the notebook and persisted as tables
or figures under `output/`.

Render the Spanish paper notebook:

``` bash
Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("notebooks/español/Cuaderno_Paper_Español.Rmd")'
```

Render the active Quarto paper:

``` bash
quarto render paper/español/quarto-tandf.qmd
```

Render the bilingual README files from their R Markdown sources:

``` bash
Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("README.Rmd", output_file = "README.md")'
Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("README.es.Rmd", output_file = "README.es.md")'
```

## Methodology {#methodology}

The methodological notebook is the main academic artifact:
[`notebooks/español/Cuaderno_Paper_Español.Rmd`](notebooks/español/Cuaderno_Paper_Español.Rmd).
It is written in Spanish and organized into numbered sections that
explain each step before running the code.

The workflow includes:

- **Data design.** Monthly tweet snapshots, market data, coverage
  audits, and explicit parameters inside the notebook.
- **Cleaning and preprocessing.** Date normalization, language
  filtering, duplicate control, text normalization, tokens, and
  reform-theme labels.
- **Weak thematic supervision.** A transparent Naive Bayes classifier
  evaluates rule-derived labels, compares against a baseline, and only
  reassigns `otros` with conservative confidence.
- **Political-discursive exploration.** Presidential tweet frequency,
  hashtags, mentions, co-mentions, word clouds, temporal term evolution,
  and `quanteda`-style network views.
- **Corpus and text models.** `quanteda` corpus, dfm, frequencies,
  keyness, collocations, lexical co-occurrences, and Wordfish.
- **Topic modeling.** `stm` topics with prevalence, semantic coherence,
  and exclusivity diagnostics.
- **Sentiment.** Spanish NRC emotions and polarity with `syuzhet`; daily
  weighted measures with `sentometrics`.
- **Econometrics.** Stationarity diagnostics, Granger tests, and VAR
  diagnostics with `lmtest`, `vars`, `tseries`, `urca`, and `sandwich`.

## Data, Coverage, and Credentials {#data-coverage-and-credentials}

The monthly tweet snapshots are treated as the reproducible source of
truth. Some snapshots are partial; inspect
[`output/tables/español/auditoria_tweets.html`](output/tables/español/auditoria_tweets.html)
before interpreting monthly dynamics.

Tweet folders are corpus-scoped. `data/raw/twitter/Opinión sobre Petro/`
contains public discussion about Petro;
`data/raw/twitter/Tweets de Gustavo Petro/` contains tweets issued by
the presidential account in `petrogustavo_full.csv`. Future searches should use parallel folders
such as `data/raw/twitter/@OtraQuery/` instead of mixing CSVs from
different emitters, queries, or methodological targets in a generic
folder.

Financial data are intentionally audited. The operational sources are
Banco de la República services: SDMX/graficador for `TRM`, BanRep/BVC
metadata for `COLCAP`, BanRep zero-coupon `TES` rates in pesos at 1, 5,
and 10 years, and the XM SINERGOX daily API for `PPPrecBolsNaci`. MSCI
and BVC are retained as methodological references for the COLCAP index,
not as the daily data feed. Each manual market refresh records
`retrieved_at`, `source_url`, `source_series_id`, `status`, and
`coverage_ratio` in the refresh audits under `output/tables/español/`. Granger/VAR
results remain **diagnostic, not conclusive**, because they test
temporal precedence rather than structural causality.

No active script in this repository reads X API credentials. Tweet
snapshots are treated as prepared inputs, and any future collection
workflow should remain manual and outside the main notebook. Do not
commit real API credentials; any previously exposed token should be
rotated before using the X API again.

## Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

| Symptom | What to check |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Missing package error | Re-run the installation block above, including `printtree` from R-universe. |
| `pandoc` not found | Install RStudio/Positron or set `RSTUDIO_PANDOC` to Quarto's Pandoc path; for example `/Applications/quarto/bin/tools/aarch64`. |
| Market coverage is missing | Check internet access, the manual BanRep updater, the endpoint/ID reference, and `output/tables/español/ingesta_mercado_fuentes.csv`; refresh market data manually if needed. |
| Tables or figures are missing | Render the notebook again after confirming the required CSVs exist in `data/processed/`. |
| README diagram is missing | Render `README.Rmd`; it regenerates `docs/assets/readme_project_flow_en.png`. |

## Credits {#credits}

This project updates and extends the original paper
`Impacto_discurso_petro__ENG_`. It uses open-source R packages for text
mining, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, visualization, tables, and
econometrics, including `quanteda`, `stm`, `sentometrics`,
`ggwordcloud`, `DiagrammeR`, and `printtree`.

Financial market series come from Banco de la República, while the
electricity price comes from XM SINERGOX. Source IDs, endpoints, and
reference URLs are documented in the scripts and in the refresh audits
under `output/tables/español/` so methodological claims stay
separate from data provenance.
